abstract: <jats:sec><jats:title>Introduction</jats:title><jats:p>Agronomic traits are key components of wheat yield. Exploitation of the major underlying quantitative trait loci (QTLs) can improve the yield potential in wheat breeding.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Methods</jats:title><jats:p>In this study, we constructed a recombinant inbred line (RIL) population from Mingxian 169 (MX169) and Pindong 34 (PD34) to determine the QTLs for grain length (GL), grain width (GW), grain length-to-width ratio (LWR), plant height (PH), spike length (SL), grain number per spike (GNS), and the thousand grain weight (TGW) across four environments using wheat 90K SNP array.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Results</jats:title><jats:p>A QTL associated with TGW, i.e., <jats:italic>QTGWpd.swust-6BS</jats:italic>, was identified on chromosome 6B, which explained approximately 14.1%–16.2% of the phenotypic variation. In addition, eight QTLs associated with GL were detected across six chromosomes in four different test environments. These were <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-1BL</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-2BL</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-3BL.1</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-3BL.2</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-5DL</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-6AL</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-6DL.1</jats:italic>, and <jats:italic>QGLpd.swust-6DL.2</jats:italic>. They accounted for 9.0%–21.3% of the phenotypic variation. Two QTLs, namely, <jats:italic>QGWpd.swust-3BS</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>QGWpd.swust-6DL</jats:italic>, were detected for GW on chromosomes 3B and 6D, respectively. These QTLs explained 12.8%–14.6% and 10.8%–15.2% of the phenotypic variation, respectively. In addition, two QTLs, i.e., <jats:italic>QLWRpd.swust-7AS.1</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>QLWRpd.swust-7AS.2</jats:italic>, were detected on chromosome 7A for the grain LWR, which explained 10.9%–11.6% and 11.6%–11.2% of the phenotypic variation, respectively. Another QTL, named <jats:italic>QGNSpd-swust-6DS</jats:italic>, was discovered on chromosome 6D, which determines the GNS and which accounted for 11.4%–13.8% of the phenotypic variation. Furthermore, five QTLs associated with PH were mapped on chromosomes 2D, 3A, 5A, 6B, and 7B. These QTLs were <jats:italic>QPHpd.swust-2DL</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QPHpd.swust-3AL</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QPHpd.swust-5AL</jats:italic>, <jats:italic>QPHpd.swust-6BL</jats:italic>, and <jats:italic>QPHpd.swust-7BS</jats:italic>, which accounted for 11.3%–19.3% of the phenotypic variation. Lastly, a QTL named <jats:italic>QSLpd.swust-3AL</jats:italic>, conferring SL, was detected on chromosome 3A and explained 16.1%–17.6% of the phenotypic variation. All of these QTLs were defined within the physical interval of the Chinese spring reference genome.</jats:p></jats:sec><jats:sec><jats:title>Discussion</jats:title><jats:p>The findings of this study have significant implications for the development of fine genetic maps, for genomic breeding, and for marker-assisted selection to enhance wheat grain yield.</jats:p></jats:sec>
